punchline: The problem on Everest was not a missing turnaround time but nobody applying it when the hour came.
thirty_sec: In May 1996 two commercial expeditions on Everest set a 2 p.m. turnaround time; on 10 May many climbers reached the summit after it. Kayes reads this as goal attachment narrowing attention in fast-changing conditions.
question: Have you written down the point where you would stop on your current goal, and who knows it?
key_contrast: A goal shows the direction; only a rule set beforehand shows when to stop.
